subject.title: [Feature]: Audio file support in read tool (multimodal parity with images)

question: Should OpenClaw add native audio attachments to the core read-tool contract, and should that be handled as part of the broader native-audio design or as a separate read-tool surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes raw local-media egress, provider routing, model content types, and session/audit behavior that require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design shared native-audio contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, opt-in policy, limits, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/audit semantics before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader tracker
options.body: Close or link this as a subcase only if maintainers explicitly decide https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51667 owns read-tool audio parity too.

options.title: Keep transcription-only for now
options.body: Leave raw audio out of the read tool and direct users to existing STT/media-understanding paths until native media egress is accepted.

recommendation.title: Design shared native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, opt-in policy, limits, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/audit semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest feature-history signal across media-understanding and the product/security boundary this decision would change.
